concepts.description_formal: For y = f(g(x)) the outer function f acts on the output of the inner function g; identifying the two parts is the precondition for applying the chain rule.
concepts.description_plain: A composite function is one function evaluated at the output of another, and it can be split into an outer and an inner part.
concepts.name: Composite function structure
concepts.notation: f of g of x; y as a function of u and u as a function of x

concepts.description_formal: If g is differentiable at x and f is differentiable at g(x), then the derivative of f composed with g at x is f prime of g of x multiplied by g prime of x; in Leibniz notation dy/dx equals dy/du times du/dx.
concepts.description_plain: The derivative of a composite is the derivative of the outer part times the derivative of the inner part.
concepts.name: Chain rule as a product of rates

concepts.description_formal: In an equation relating x and y, differentiating a term in y with respect to x produces the derivative of that term with respect to y multiplied by dy/dx, which is the chain rule applied to the implicitly defined function.
concepts.description_plain: When y depends on x, every y term differentiates with an extra dy/dx factor because the chain rule applies to y as well.
concepts.name: A dependent variable inside an equation
concepts.notation: d/dx of y to the n equals n times y to the n minus one times dy/dx

concepts.description_formal: The differentiated equation is linear in dy/dx, so collecting the dy/dx terms, factoring, and dividing produces an expression for dy/dx that generally involves both x and y.
concepts.description_plain: After differentiating both sides, the dy/dx terms are collected on one side and factored out to isolate dy/dx.
concepts.name: Solving a differentiated relation for dy/dx
concepts.notation: dy/dx expressed as a quotient in x and y

concepts.description_formal: A point on an implicitly defined curve has a horizontal tangent when dy/dx equals zero there and a vertical tangent when the expression for dy/dx is undefined there; the candidate must satisfy the original equation as well as the condition on dy/dx.
concepts.description_plain: A horizontal tangent needs the numerator of dy/dx to vanish and a vertical tangent needs the denominator to vanish, and in both cases the point must also lie on the curve.
concepts.name: Tangent line behaviour on an implicit curve
concepts.notation: dy/dx equals zero; denominator of dy/dx equals zero

concepts.description_formal: If f is differentiable and invertible with g the inverse of f, and f prime of g of a is not zero, then g prime of a equals one divided by f prime of g of a; the result follows from differentiating f of g of x equals x.
concepts.description_plain: The slope of an inverse function at a point is the reciprocal of the slope of the original function at the matching point.
concepts.name: Derivative of an inverse function
concepts.notation: g prime of a equals one over f prime of g of a

concepts.description_formal: The derivatives of the inverse sine, inverse cosine, and inverse tangent functions follow from the inverse function derivative rule together with a Pythagorean identity, and composing with an inner function multiplies the formula by the derivative of that inner function.
concepts.description_plain: Each inverse trigonometric function has a fixed derivative formula, and a composite version carries an extra factor from the inside.
concepts.name: Derivatives of inverse trigonometric functions
concepts.notation: derivative of arctan u equals u prime over one plus u squared

concepts.description_formal: An expression is classified by its outermost structure as a sum, a constant multiple, a product, a quotient, a composition, or a basic named function, and that classification selects the first rule to apply; nested structure selects the rules that follow.
concepts.description_plain: The outermost operation of an expression decides which differentiation rule opens the work.
concepts.name: Classification of an expression before differentiating
concepts.notation: outermost operation; order of rule application

concepts.description_formal: Differentiating f prime produces the second derivative f double prime provided the derivative of f prime exists, and repeating the process produces higher-order derivatives of f.
concepts.description_plain: Differentiating a derivative gives the next derivative, and the process repeats as long as each derivative exists.
concepts.name: Repeated differentiation
concepts.notation: f double prime; f superscript n

concepts.description_formal: For y equal to f of x the second derivative is written d squared y over d x squared, f double prime of x, or y double prime, and the nth derivative is written d to the n y over d x to the n or f superscript n of x.
concepts.description_plain: The same higher derivative can be written in prime notation or in Leibniz notation, and the two must be read interchangeably.
concepts.name: Notation for higher-order derivatives
concepts.notation: d squared y over d x squared; f superscript n of x

prerequisites.description_plain: Reading a formula such as a power of a trigonometric expression and naming which operation is applied last and which is applied first.

prerequisites.description_plain: Collecting like terms in an unknown that appears in several places, factoring it out, and dividing to isolate it.

prerequisites.description_plain: Producing exact values of sine, cosine, and tangent, and converting between a trigonometric ratio and the sides of a right triangle.

prerequisites.description_plain: Recognising that f prime of x, dy/dx, d squared y over d x squared, and y double prime name derivatives, and writing the operator separately from the result.

prerequisites.notes: Non-calculus prerequisite inferred from the demands of the essential knowledge statements for this unit.

prerequisites.description_plain: Combining fractions, cancelling common factors, and rewriting radicals as powers without changing the value of the expression.

prerequisites.notes: Non-calculus prerequisite inferred from the demands of the essential knowledge statements for this unit.

prerequisites.description_plain: Setting a numerator or a denominator equal to zero, solving, and checking which candidate values are admissible.
